name: Supply tightness heatmap
note: How tight each layer of the chain is, in the suppliers' own words — and until WHEN. Layers sorted roughly upstream → downstream.

tables.title: Sold out / allocated until
rows: Supply very tight; 2026 capex RAISED to $60-64bn, +$100bn additional Arizona investment, 13 new Taiwan fabs, 3 new N3 fabs; 'no bottlenecks' seen to expansion
Constraint = ADVANCED-NODE availability for SoCs (not memory)
2027 Low-NA EUV close to FULLY COVERED with orders; significant 2028 orders already booked (~2 yrs ahead); capacity +30% in 2027 for both Low-NA EUV and immersion, further +30% under study for 2028

'Packaging capacity is SO TIGHT that now it's LIMITING MY CUSTOMERS' GROWTH' (C.C. Wei) — TSMC welcomes rival EMIB-T taking overflow; +$100bn Arizona includes adv-packaging fabs; 10-20% of 2026 capex to packaging/test/mask
AI packaging set to TRIPLE but pace limited by customer ramps AND component supply
Fulfillment rate at RECORD LOW; customers pulling 2027 demand forward
Both supply-constrained; cleanroom scarcity + HBM trade ratio; NAND cleanroom redirected to DRAM
Installed wafer capacity -20%+ from prior peak by end-2026 → greenfield needed

Allocation economics showing up in P&L: FQ4 non-GAAP gross margin hit 52.7% and FQ1'27 guided to a sharp step-up ($4.1bn rev / $7.30 EPS); nearline capacity almost fully allocated through CY2027; momentum 'continuing in 2027'
52-week chip lead times + reservations beyond; shortages a '1-2 year phenomenon'
Largely sold out 2026; already allocating 2027 capacity; GPU pricing up across generations
Industry 2027 capacity 'already extremely scarce', pushing into 2028
ALL operational capacity fully contracted — 'racing to build supply'
Constraint rank: DRAM > NAND > CPUs > HDDs; leading-edge lead times ~1 year
Supply TIGHT all H1-26 ('much of this demand was unforecasted'); raising wafer/back-end/substrate capacity; chiplets ease 2nm wafer needs; 2027 supply expected better than 2026

Industry 'MEANINGFULLY UNDERSUPPLIED' rolling into 2027; 8-10 new fabs online by end-2027, customers ordering fab-fill equipment at LEAD TIME OR BEYOND; CY26 WFE raised to low-$150B only because customers squeezed extra clean-room space; down payments rebounded (+$213M deferred rev)
116GW contracted (->125+ by YE2026); mostly SOLD OUT through 2030, >half of 2031's 30GW sold by year-end; agreements signed into 2031
US data-center backlog 228GW = 12 YEARS at 2025 build rates
CY2026 industry bit growth only high-10s% because SUPPLY-CONSTRAINED; CY2027 demand expected to EXCEED supply
AI power business ON ALLOCATION — demand strongly exceeds supply; converting + ramping capacity (AI power rev EUR 1.5B -> 2.5B FY2027)
Demand > supply: Taiwan-earthquake wafer shortfall + industry-wide TESTER shortage leaving wafers idle; price hikes likely
N3 capacity "the most precious thing in the industry"; wafer+CoWoS turnaround 6-7 months caps 2026 upside; wafer (not CoWoS) is the bottleneck
SAP substrate demand to EXCEED industry supply capacity; Ibiden cannot expand beyond plan through fiscal 2028 (people/lead-time limits)
ABF SOLD OUT at all three; quotes +5-10% QoQ from Q2 2026, spot prices +30%+
HB capacity raised 15/mo -> 250/yr; ~6-month lead times; AP7 program ~100 bonders "may be significantly higher"
Pipeline REVISED DOWN from 43 GW to 36 GW after Transmission Security Agreements + COLLATERAL requirements 'weeded out speculative projects'; capex only where 'certain and durable'
Test utilization back to 80% (IDM capex turning point); Cohu doubling Malaysia output by year-end with another step up mid-2027; Aehr says it is NOT capacity limited even at $150M revenue

US optical-connectivity manufacturing capacity expanding 10x + US fiber production +>50% under the NVIDIA long-term partnership for AI factories; Amazon multiyear multibillion fiber agreement joins Meta's up-to-$6B deal

Customers placing LONG-TERM orders 'to secure supply in a constrained environment' (AI & cloud intake EUR 2.8bn); vertically integrating InP — San Jose fab to volume production end-2026, NXP Arizona site acquired, Pennsylvania test/packaging capacity 10x

'Demand continues to OUTPACE SUPPLY no matter how fast we add capacity'; backlog well over $100M; InP revenue on track to MORE THAN TRIPLE by end-2026; capacity 2x 2026 (ahead of schedule) + 2x again 2027; China export-permit timing still gates recognized revenue
Back-end supply environment constrained amid "unprecedented demand" (mitigated via vertical integration); >80% of $7.7B hardware backlog converts within 12mo

tables.title: Demand destruction from the squeeze (the other side)
rows: The squeeze landed: Qualcomm FQ3 handset revenue $5.09bn, DOWN 20% YoY, in a 'challenging memory and supply environment'; broad-based input-cost inflation across wafer/assembly/test/packaging/memory with PRICING ACTIONS being taken to pass it through
Unit TAM seen down low-double-digits 2026 on memory costs (Micron, Intel, Silicon Motion all flag it)
Micron Q2 / Intel Q1 / SiMo Q1 FY2026
High memory cost makes low-cost phones uneconomical through 2026-27
KLA: DRAM in its image-processing computers = ~100bps GM headwind thru CY2026
TDK FY2027 assumptions: smartphone production -10%, notebooks -12%, tablets -8% on the memory-price shock — while AI server boards +21% and nearline HDD +7%
Kioxia: nearline-HDD replacement running SLOWER in CY26 than first expected — customers prioritize high-performance AI-inference SSDs (TAM still expanding)
SUMCO: memory shortages are CURBING wafer demand from non-leading-edge logic customers (shortage spillover)
3M: consumer-electronics demand soft on industry-wide memory-chip issues, while semis/data-center electronics orders are up double digits
